title: Timber Acoustic

excluded_sources.reason: grey preview of the old LEGO model

gate_a.note: The variant has no usable street view: variant_2.png has the same bytes as the old LEGO family preview (hash prefix b33e3a3378be). The oblique and roof views agree and are the authority. A person must rule on this before activation, as for the crescent and the laneway.

measurement_contract.scale_basis: No image carries a scale. The podium outline in the roof view (888 by 650 px) is set to 88 by 64.4 m, matching the archetype's suggested 90 by 65 m footprint and 1.4:1 aspect. Plan positions are measured in the roof view at 0.0991 m/px. Heights: a pinhole camera fitted to 39 traced podium points in the oblique (31 px RMS) barely changes between an 11 m and a 21 m podium, so the podium takes the catalogue's two 5 m floors (glazed ground floor to 6.0 m, finned band to 11.2 m). The shell rims are set from the same fit, peaking near 23.6 m (west) and 21.6 m (east).

oblique: High view from the south over the front plaza toward the water and mountains.

Rounded podium wrapped in close vertical bronze fins above a glazed ground floor with cafe tables inside; the glazing is about as tall as the band; a horizontal window slot in the band at the west end.
Planted roof garden with winding pale paths and a thin dark edge.
Two opposing curved shells clad in bronze battens, their outer walls leaning in: the west shell rises highest at the north-west, the east shell at the north-east; their rims meet in a V at the back.
Inside the west shell a narrow sloping ring runs round the oculus below its stepped inner edge: the east sheet continuing underneath.
An oval oculus between them shows the auditorium: timber walls, raked seating, balcony fronts and a stage.
top: Near-nadir view, north up, the pier to the west and south.
Podium a rounded rectangle about 888 by 650 px; roof garden with a winding path loop and planting.
Shells spiral round an oval oculus about 235 by 185 px, centred 114 px east of the podium centre: the west shell wraps west and south, the east shell north-east and east; a radial notch at the north.
Inside the oculus, seating rows on the west half facing a dark stage on the east.

source_conflicts: variant_2.png, the street view, is the grey preview of the old LEGO model, not a picture of this building. It is excluded; the oblique and roof views govern. Needs a ruling by a person.
The oblique puts the oculus about 3.5 m east of the podium centre, the roof view 11.3 m. The roof view governs plan positions; the oblique governs heights.
The catalogue text says "two opposing curved planes in weathered bronze-tone metal with landscaped rooftop terrace". The images agree; the title "Timber Acoustic" refers to the interior and battens.
hidden_assumptions: The north and east elevations are seen only obliquely or from above; their ground floor continues the glazing, with an opaque back-of-house and a service door at the north-east (inferred).
The oculus is glazed (clear) so the hall is closed; the images show its interior without glass reflections.
Roof access is a stair inside the west shell, entered from the roof garden through a portal cut into its south-west foot (inferred; no access is visible in the images).

Interiors are schematic: a foyer with cafe tables, counters and columns round the hall drum, with three doors into it; a stair from the west foyer to a closed upper storey of rooms that runs right round behind the band; the auditorium, only as large as the oculus, with 11 raked tiers (about 340 stalls seats), two balcony rings, a stage and choir terraces.
The pier, the stepped terrace to the west, the water, boats, cars and people belong to the site and are not modelled.

roof_contract.form: two spiral sheets about an oval oculus, rising from its lip to high outer rims, with outer walls leaning in to the roof garden; the east sheet runs on under the west as a ring on the lip, and the west sheet steps up over it at the north notch
roof_contract.weathering: each sheet is one closed surface with standing seams; the lip and oculus glazing close the centre

identity_contract: rounded-rectangle podium, about 1.37:1, wrapped in close vertical bronze fins over a recessed glazed ground floor
planted roof garden with a winding path loop
two opposing spiral shells clad in bronze battens
a stepped notch where the shells meet at the north
an oval oculus revealing raked seating and a stage

contact_contract.ground: a 6 m plaza apron round the podium; nothing below grade
